What's striking is how the sheer scale gets lost in the noise - 25M+ on the verge of food insecurity, the world's largest displacement crisis, and it barely registers in Western coverage. The RSF-SAF dynamic is underappreciated: this isn't just a civil war, it's a contest between two factions that both emerged from the same predatory state apparatus. The ICC warrants against al-Bashir going unexecuted for 15+ years tells you everything about the enforcement gap in international accountability. Economic collapse is the silent multiplier - when healthcare infrastructure is essentially gone and local civil society orgs are among the last functioning institutions, the long-term reconstruction cost becomes almost incalculable. Thanks Vox for covering this seriously.
